### Observed differences

- The preferred successor of A11 flipped. In the earlier window, about 5 in 10 of A11's outgoing transitions led to A13 and about 2 in 10 to A12; in the later window only about 1 in 4 led to A13 while about 4 in 10 led to A12 — a profile difference larger than in roughly 995 of 1,000 random re-splits, based on 90–97 outgoing transitions per window. [DIR011]
- The A12/A13 handover reversed in step: A13→A12 fell from about 5 in 10 to 3 in 10 of A13's outgoing transitions while A13→A11 rose from 2 in 10 to 1 in 3 [DIR013]; A12→A13 rose from about 2 in 10 to 3.5 in 10 [DIR012]; and A03 now feeds A13 more often than A11 (A03→A13 26→39, A03→A11 40→32 per 100). [DIR003]
- Participation of A11, A12 and A13 barely moved: each ran in about 45–46 of 100 traces before and 48–49 of 100 after, differences well within what random re-splits produce. [OCC011, OCC012, OCC013]
- A19 and A20 exchanged their preference after A44: A44→A19 rose from 43 to about 52 in 100 while A44→A20 fell from 54 to 47; A19 ran in 53 of 100 traces (was 46) and A20 in 47 (was 55). [DIR043, OCC019, OCC020]
- A42 and A43 are executed more often and repeat more: A43's mean rose from 0.72 to 0.86 per trace (participation 44→51 of 100 traces, repetition 17→21), A42's mean from 0.28 to 0.35; A42→A43 is now essentially A42's only outgoing transition, and A43→A42 rose from 37 to 41 in 100 while A43→A44 fell from 62 to 56. [OCC039, OCC040, DIR041, DIR042]
- Several further local reroutings of existing paths: A01 shifted share from A05 to A09 (38→25 and 29→38 per 100) while A07 shifted the opposite way (A05 30→41, A09 35→25) [DIR001, DIR007]; the pairs A37/A38 and A39/A40 reversed their mutual preference and shifted share to and from A32 [DIR036, DIR037, DIR038, DIR039]; in the A21–A24/A31 group, A24→A21 rose from 19 to 32 per 100 and A23 and A24 moved oppositely in participation (47→53 vs 54→47 of 100 traces) [DIR020, DIR021, DIR022, DIR023, OCC023, OCC024]; A06 (35→27) and A18 (32→27 of 100 traces) participate less [OCC006, OCC018]. Apparent successor-profile overhauls at A02, A04, A08, A10 and A50 rest on only 6–10 outgoing transitions per window and carry little weight. [DIR002, DIR004, DIR008, DIR010, DIR049]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a reversal of the traversal order through A11, A12 and A13. In the earlier window the dominant chain was A11 → A13 → A12 (A13 followed about half of A11's outgoing transitions, and A12 followed A13 in about half of A13's); in the later window the dominant chain is A11 → A12 → A13 (A11→A12 about 4 in 10, A12→A13 about 3.5 in 10), with A13 handing back to A11 or exiting to A14, and A03 feeding A13 more often than A11. The three successor profiles changed in mutually consistent directions, each difference ranking above roughly 88–99.5 of 100 random re-splits on 90–98 outgoing transitions per window, while participation of all three activities stayed at 45–49 of 100 traces — so the change lies in the routing between existing activities, not in how often they run. Limitations: only control-flow evidence is available (no relational or positional items), DIR shares are over outgoing transitions rather than cases, and similar preference reversals appear at other activity pairs, so the evidence cannot rule out that this reversal is one facet of a broader re-routing of existing paths rather than a change confined to A11, A12 and A13. [DIR011, DIR012, DIR013, DIR003, OCC011, OCC012, OCC013]

Other differences: A42 and A43 occur and repeat more often, with more A43→A42 handbacks [OCC039, OCC040, DIR041, DIR042]; A19 gained and A20 lost share both after A44 and in overall participation [DIR043, OCC019, OCC020]; A06 and A18 participate less often [OCC006, OCC018]; and several other local successor-share shifts (A01/A05/A07/A09, the A21–A24/A31 group, A25/A27/A35/A36/A41, A31→A37–A40, A46→A45/A49) point in varied directions that this evidence does not tie to a single underlying difference. [DIR001, DIR007, DIR020, DIR021, DIR022, DIR023, DIR024, DIR030, DIR034, DIR035, DIR045]
